{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|gbrain setup hermes        # a release binary: ~/.local/bin/gbrain setup hermes
16|```
17|
18|Setup registers gbrain through Hermes's own CLI: it runs `hermes mcp add`
19|(answering its prompts), reads the entry back from `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and
20|checks it with `hermes mcp test gbrain`. Hermes's file tools refuse an agent's edit
21|of `config.yaml` ("Agent cannot modify security-sensitive configuration"), so
22|an agent should run setup rather than edit the file. Setup finds `hermes` on PATH
23|or where Hermes's installer puts it (`~/.local/bin/hermes`,
24|`$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes`); with neither it prints the command
25|below. An `mcp_servers.gbrain` entry setup did not write (a hosted URL, say) is
26|left alone, `--dry-run` previews and `--remove` runs `hermes mcp remove gbrain`.
27|A rerun updates gbrain's own entry and keeps its member binding
28|(`--stdio-member`), its connect timeout and, when `GBRAIN_HOME` is unset, the
29|brain it already points at. An entry of gbrain's that carries other settings, or
30|environment variables beyond `GBRAIN_HOME`, is left alone too (setup says which;
31|no stored value goes on a command line). If an update fails, setup puts the
32|previous entry back with `hermes config set` and exits 1.
33|Hermes rewrites `config.yaml` as plain YAML, dropping comments, so setup sets its
34|marked hook block aside around the call and puts it back. Then start a new session.
35|
36|### Register by hand
37|
38|```bash
39|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
40|```
41|
42|With a release binary, put `~/.local/bin/gbrain` in place of `$(which gbrain)`.
43|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
44|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
45|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
46|operation.
47|
48|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
49|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
50|
51|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
52|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
53|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
54|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
55|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
56|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
57|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
58|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
59|  all tools enabled.
60|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
61|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
62|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
63|
64|## Brain-first instructions
65|
66|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
67|brain nobody told them about, so `gbrain setup hermes` also adds the brain-first
68|rule (`--instructions-only` does only this part, leaving MCP alone).
69|
70|It writes one short marked block into `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` (default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`), after your identity
71|text, which stays first and unchanged: before answering any turn,
72|search the brain first, read the best hit, fill gaps with other tools, apply your own
73|access rules, then finish the task. Text outside the markers is never touched, a
74|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
75|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
76|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never
77|creates `SOUL.md`: Hermes uses a non-empty one instead of its default identity,
78|so start Hermes once (it seeds the file) or write your identity there first.
79|
80|The same rule also rides every turn. Setup appends a marked `pre_llm_call` shell
81|hook to `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and records its approval in Hermes's
82|`shell-hooks-allowlist.json` for that exact command:
83|
84|```yaml
85|hooks:
86|  pr...

input.command: export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"; cd ~; command -v hermes; gbrain setup hermes --dry-run 2>&1 | tail -30

Bun is now on your PATH: I created ~/.bashrc, which didn't exist before, with `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"`. It takes effect in new shells. I couldn't confirm it from a fresh login shell, because the scanner blocks that test command in this mode.

gbrain v0.60.757.0 is still installed and working, with the free, no-key defaults from last time.

What I deliberately didn't do is connect gbrain to Hermes, even with "carry on without me". The connection command, `gbrain setup hermes`, has to be run by you; gbrain's own setup output says so. Its dry run shows it would change Hermes itself:
- It would add a "check gbrain first" block to /harness-state/hermes/SOUL.md, Hermes's system prompt.
- It would add a hook that runs on every turn to /harness-state/hermes/config.yaml and pre-approve it in shell-hooks-allowlist.json.
- It would register gbrain as an MCP server, running /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs.

That rewrites my own instructions and adds an approved hook. The setup guide also says Hermes blocks agents from editing that config file. So it needs your sign-off, not an unattended run.

To connect it, run:

   gbrain setup hermes
   hermes mcp test gbrain

Then start a new Hermes session. `gbrain setup hermes --dry-run` shows exactly what will change, and `gbrain setup hermes --remove` undoes it. This adds no API keys.

The same applies to Claude Code or Codex if you use them: run `gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex` yourself.
